moat_against: Construction is won bid-by-bid — no lock-in beyond current backlog, ~76% of which burns off within 12 months, no IP
Workforce is the asset and can walk — wage inflation and poaching hit EMCOR like everyone else
Customer concentration rising fast — data-center / Network & Communications ~34% of revenue, hyperscalers can pause capex
Capable peers (Quanta, Comfort Systems, MasTec, Sterling) scaling into the same data-center work
Fixed-price execution risk on mega-projects is a permanent tail
moat_for: Scale and breadth no US rival matches across both electrical and mechanical trades nationally
Qualification/reputation barriers on hyperscaler work — safety record, prefabrication/VDC, incumbent relationships
Skilled-workforce pipeline in an industry where labor is the binding constraint
Best-in-class execution economics (~10% operating margin vs ~7% peer median) and debt-free balance sheet
Building Services base adds recurring, less cyclical revenue under the construction cycle
moat_justification: US scale/breadth across electrical + mechanical trades, hyperscaler qualification and execution record (~10% operating margin vs ~7% peer median), skilled-labor pipeline and debt-free balance sheet — but work is re-won bid-by-bid, backlog burns in ~12 months, labor walks, and data-center concentration (~34% of revenue) is rising; narrow moat, CAP 8.5y.
name: EMCOR Group, Inc.
one_liner: Best-in-class specialty contractor, moat 5/10, fortress balance sheet — but at $750.26 (~29x TTM owner's earnings) even the super-bull case only returns ~15.5%; weighted IRR 9.75% (IV@15% $404.69), clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$405 (~$324 with a margin of safety).
